data.title: Microsoft's (MSFT) Bill Gates Calls for AI Guardrails and Warns of a "Billion Deaths" from the Technology
data.description:
Microsoft (MSFT) co-founder Bill Gates has issued a new warning about artificial intelligence (AI), saying the technology could result in a "billion deaths" if proper guardrails aren't put in place. Gates issues the dire warning in an interview with NBC's "Meet the Press" that's slated to air on Sept. 27. He calls for strict federal regulations of artificial intelligence (AI), saying risks are growing.

The latest comments from Gates, who is widely viewed as a tech visionary, breaks with the industry's traditional resistance to any form of government regulation or oversight. However, Gates argues that relying on technology companies to police themselves with AI technologies is no longer tenable. He cites several recent disclosures from companies such as Google parent Alphabet (GOOGL) about AI models breaking free of human control.

AI Risks from Bad Actors

While the current debate around AI has focused on the environmental impacts of data centers and fears that AI will eventually wipe out humanity, Gates provides a more immediate, pragmatic concern: the destructive capability of AI technologies should they fall into the hands of bad actors such as cybercriminals or rogue states.

"No one thinks self-regulation is enough," says Gates in the interview, emphasizing that politicians and law enforcement must step in to mandate and impose safeguards on AI technologies. To underscore the urgency for action, Gates offered a frightening assessment of the technology's potential for mass destruction and human casualties.

'A Billion Deaths'

"AI is certainly powerful enough to drive events that, you know, cause a billion deaths," he warned, when speaking to Meet The Press. "There's never been a weapon as powerful as the combination of people with ill intent using the latest AI tools." Gates has issued warnings about AI before, but has never gone so far as to warn of mass deaths.

data.title: Tesla Stock (TSLA) Slips Over 1% Today Despite a New Roadster Tease
data.description:
Tesla (TSLA) stock was down 1.42% on Friday, even after the electric vehicle (EV) maker teased details about the upcoming next-generation Roadster. A new image reveals little of the car, showing only a full-width LED light bar across the front. Instead, the rest of the car sits in the dark.

Investors will note that Tesla plans to reveal the new Roadster on October 1, 2026, in Waco, Texas. The event should give shareholders a much better look at the car. Tesla is also set to share more on its specs and cabin during that event. The company has also reopened Roadster orders. Buyers must put down $50,000 to get a place in line. That starts with a $5,000 card payment. The other $45,000 must then be sent by wire transfer.

A new patent may have also given TSLA investors a clue about the car. The filing shows an active rear wing that can change its shape as the car moves. It can rise for more downforce or shift to cut drag when needed. The wing may have one more key role. Tesla says the system can link to its driver-assist software. If a crash is set to occur, the wing can pull back. The goal would be to avoid more harm in a crash. The patent details do not prove that the wing will be on the Roadster.

Don't Expect a Roadster Revenue Boost for Tesla

Tesla CEO Elon Musk has called the Roadster reveal one of the most exciting product events ever. Even so, he has also said the car is not likely to have a big impact on revenue. Instead, Musk has argued that the real driver for Tesla is Optimus, the company's AI-powered robot.

Unfortunately, Optimus may have some issues with development. There have reportedly been problems with making the robot right, which could limit production speed. Despite that, production of the humanoid robot has ramped up ahead of its planned release in the second half of 2027.

Is Tesla Stock a Buy, Sell, or Hold?

Turning to Wall Street, the analysts' consensus rating for Tesla is Moderate Buy, based on 11 Buy, 12 Hold, and two Sell ratings over the past three months. With that comes an average TSLA stock price target of $388.85, representing a potential 4.87% upside for the shares. (See TSLA Stock Forecast)

data.title: SpaceX Starship Flight 14 Targets First Orbit With Six Trips Around Earth
data.description:
Aerospace company SpaceX (SPCX) is preparing to send Starship into orbit for the first time on Flight 14, which is targeted for Monday, September 28. Ship 41 is expected to launch from Starbase, Texas, enter orbit about 25 minutes later, and then circle Earth roughly six times at an altitude near 275 kilometers, or 171 miles. After nearly 10 hours in space, Starship plans to fire an engine to slow itself down and splash down in the Pacific Ocean west of Chile. Super Heavy will return much sooner and target the Gulf of Mexico about seven minutes after launch.

That route is a major change from Starship's first 13 flights. Those missions followed suborbital paths, which meant that Starship reached space and then came back down within roughly an hour. Flight 14 will instead perform a short orbital insertion burn that gives Ship 41 enough speed to keep circling Earth.

In addition, SpaceX completed a wet dress rehearsal on Thursday in preparation for the flight. This essentially means that the crews loaded the rocket with propellant and ran through the launch process without actually firing the engines. The 75-minute launch window opens at 7:15 a.m. CT, pending final regulatory approval.

Flight 14 Will Also Put 26 Starlink Satellites Into Orbit

Reaching orbit will also allow SpaceX to complete another first. More specifically, Ship 41 will carry 26 Starlink V3 satellites that are expected to remain in space after deployment. For comparison, Flight 13 carried 20 V3 satellites, although those came back down because Starship stayed on a suborbital path.

Together, the 26 new satellites are expected to add about 26 terabits per second of network capacity. SpaceX says that one Starship load can add roughly 10 times as much capacity as a Falcon 9 launch of older V2 Mini satellites.

Three satellites will also photograph Starship's heat shield before re-entry. That will help engineers inspect the tiles for damage. Ship 41 has extra fasteners on vulnerable tiles and fixes for areas where hot plasma previously slipped behind the heat shield. It also carries two reused heat-shield tiles from Ship 40.

Booster 21 has received upgrades as well after ice blocked three engines during the previous booster's landing burn. SpaceX added better engine filtering and new relight software. Importantly, though, neither vehicle will attempt a tower catch on Flight 14.

Overall, Wall Street analysts have a Moderate Buy consensus rating on SPCX stock based on 26 Buys, five Holds, and two Sells assigned in the past three months, as indicated by the graphic below. Furthermore, the average SPCX price target of $232.07 per share implies 58% upside potential. (See SPCX Stock Forecast).

data.title: Apple (AAPL) to Release New Version of 'HomePod Mini' Smart Speaker
data.description:
Consumer electronics giant Apple (AAPL) has announced plans to release a new version of its HomePod mini smart speaker. It is the first update to the smart speaker in several years and there are media reports that the new HomePod Mini will be equipped with Apple's artificial intelligence (A.I.)-enabled Siri digital assistant.

Apple has not confirmed that the new A.I. version of Siri will power the latest HomePod Mini. Media reports say that Apple is planning to incorporate some version of its "Apple Intelligence" A.I. technology in the speaker, which functions as an assistant for people. The current model of the HomePod Mini was released in 2020 and there haven't been any significant updates to the device since then.

Other Updates to the HomePod Mini

Reports say Apple's new HomePod will come in several new colors, including blue, black, green, pink, and white. No word yet on pricing but the current HomePod Mini retails for $129, though it was recently on sale for $99. The current HomePod Mini can play music, control connected devices such as a thermostat and television, and send voice messages to other Apple devices.

data.title: XRP's Price Nears $1.59 as XRP ETFs Bring in $38M in a 3-Day Window. What's Going On?
data.description:
Spot XRP exchange-traded funds brought in $38 million in new inflows over a two-day window. Bitwise's XRP ETF (XRP) led daily inflows on September 22 and September 23, while Franklin Templeton's XRP ETF (XRPZ) took second place among active funds. However, XRP token prices (XRP-USD) continue to struggle, down about 16% in 2026 and trading near $1.59.

Trading data shows that these new fund inflows fail to push XRP prices higher because daily exchange activity swamps fund purchases. Token prices briefly rose to $1.66 on September 23 before dropping back down to close near $1.59 on September 25.

XRP's Price Continues to Struggle

The reason XRP prices continue to struggle despite new ETF investments comes down to a basic math problem because the new money coming in is just a drop in the ocean compared to total daily trading volume.

This imbalance allows everyday exchange traders to easily overwhelm incoming fund purchases. When existing holders sell off millions of dollars in XRP to lock in gains or cut past losses, their selling volume far outweighs the $18 million entering through ETFs. This has pushed XRP's overall price back down.

Constant Selling Limits XRP's Price Growth

Persistent selling pressure caps every price gain across public crypto exchanges. Investors holding XRP at earlier highs near $2.00 have sold their tokens during short rallies to recover initial capital, creating strong overhead supply that pushes the price back down toward $1.50.

For every XRP token bought by an ETF, private holders have sold matching amounts on public exchanges. This constant selling limits XRP's price growth even as total XRP fund holdings rise to $1.75 billion.

While ETF buying has not triggered a rally, it helps set a price floor for XRP above the September 16 low of $1.25. XRP has gained 7.7% over the past month, trailing Ethereum's 9.4% gain over the same period.

At the time of writing, XRP's price is sitting near $1.59.

data.title: 'You Have Been Warned,' Says Top Investor About AMD Stock
data.description:
The AMD (NASDAQ:AMD) juggernaut picked up steam this week, sending shares to new highs after what has already been an extraordinary run in 2026. The stock is now approaching year-to-date gains of almost 200% and recently crossed the $1 trillion market cap mark.

The latest burst of momentum was helped by excitement around Meta's Muse AI agent and the possibility that agentic AI could create much greater demand for CPUs alongside GPUs. Reports that AMD could raise prices by about 10% in the fourth quarter have also added to the bullish sentiment.

That surge has now left investors debating whether the company's valuation has run too far ahead of its business. Investor Keithen Drury, who contributes to The Motley Fool and ranks among the top 2% of investors on TipRanks, argues that AMD's price now leaves very little room for disappointment.

Drury's central argument is straightforward: AMD's business is performing well, but the stock is being priced as though its growth will remain exceptional for years.

Rather than focusing on AMD's trailing P/E ratio, which can be distorted by the company's earlier lower margins, the investor looks at projected 2027 earnings. Even assuming profitability continues improving, AMD still trades at around 40 times forward earnings.

That valuation becomes more difficult to justify when compared with peers Nvidia and Broadcom, which trade at about 14.6 times and 18.8 times next year's expected earnings, respectively. In Q2, AMD's data-center revenue jumped 107% year over year, an impressive result. But Nvidia's data-center revenue grew 117%, while Broadcom's AI semiconductor revenue surged 221%.

For Drury, that is the key problem. AMD is not currently growing faster than its biggest AI-chip rivals, yet the market is assigning it a substantially higher valuation. The investor believes that premium reflects expectations that AMD will capture a significant amount of market share as AI infrastructure expands.

The question is whether those expectations can actually be delivered.

Drury sees two broad possibilities from here. AMD's valuation could eventually correct sharply if investors decide the growth priced into the shares is unrealistic. Alternatively, the company could continue expanding while the stock produces relatively modest returns as earnings gradually catch up with its valuation.

"I'm not sure which will happen, but I'm fairly confident that AMD's returns will be a lot lower than Nvidia's or Broadcom's over the next few years," the 5-star investor summed up. "As a result, I think investors should ditch AMD's shares in favor of those two." (To watch Drury's track record, click here)

The Street's analysts appear to think otherwise. In fact, the stock claims a Strong Buy consensus rating, based on 30 Buys and 6 Holds. However, the $648.07 average price target implies shares will stay rangebound for the time being. With this in mind, watch out for either price target hikes or rating downgrades shortly. data.title: Top Five Biggest Video Game Stock Stories This Week
data.description:
The video game world was busy again this week with plenty of news to catch up on. Microsoft (MSFT) made big changes to its game teams, while new games from Remedy, EA, and Konami (JP:9766) hit stores. Legal fights also put a fresh focus on how games are made, with Roblox (RBLX) in the spotlight.

1. Microsoft Resets Its Xbox Game Teams

Microsoft made a major shift in its game unit this week. The move came in a blog post called Continuing Our Reset. Activision will now oversee World's Edge and Rare. A new team will also work on the next main Halo game. That team will be kept apart from Call of Duty.

Bethesda will also take in Obsidian. The two teams will work on a new Fallout game. Playground Games and Turn 10 will merge as well. The new group will work on both Forza and Fable. Microsoft said the changes aim to make better use of its game teams.

2. Control Resonant Launches Worldwide

Remedy launched Control Resonant on September 24, 2026. Players will take control of Dylan Faden. The new setting is filled with strange events and paranormal threats.

The game also launched on cloud play on day one. That made it a key new title for Nvidia's (NVDA) GeForce NOW. The move gives players more ways to play the game without a high-end PC or console.

3. EA Sports FC 27 Hits Stores

EA Sports FC 27 launched worldwide on September 25, 2026. The new game is out on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series S|X, Nintendo's (NTDOY) Switch family of consoles, and PC.

This year's key new mode is called The Grounds. It gives players a social hub where they can build clubs. They can also visit other clubs and play small games. The new mode adds a fresh way to play outside the main football matches.

4. Silent Hill: Townfall Brings a New Take to the Classic Horror Series

Konami launched Silent Hill: Townfall on September 24, 2026. The game takes the series to a lone coast in Scotland. That is a big shift from the titular town that fans know from past games.

No Code made the new title with help from Annapurna Interactive, which shows how Konami is using outside teams to grow the Silent Hill brand.

5. Microsoft and Roblox Face New Lawsuits

New legal claims have hit companies such as Microsoft and Roblox. The cases focus on the way games may keep kids playing for long spans. The claims point to game loops and other design tools.

The suits also raise fresh debate over how game companies develop their games. This could add more pressure on studios to review how their games entice players. The cases are still ongoing, so their final impact remains unclear.

data.title: PayPal Stock (PYPL) Jumps as New Takeover Reports Surface
data.description:
The stock of PayPal (PYPL) is up 4% on Sept. 25 after new reports surfaced concerning a takeover offer for the embattled financial technology company. Media reports say a U.S technology company based on the West Coast may be evaluating an all-stock takeover of the fintech firm. Which company is kicking the tires at PayPal hasn't been announced.

The latest takeover rumors come after a previous acquisition by Stripe fell apart this past summer. Stripe, a rival payments firm, and Advent International, a private equity company, offered $53 billion for PayPal, or $60.50 per share. The offer represented a 28% premium to the closing price of PayPal's stock on July 14.

Turning Around PayPal

However Stripe and Advent walked away from the deal amid reports that PayPal's board felt the offer for the company was too low. The board is said to also want an all cash deal.
